analysis:
Scope: console-ui device-code approval only. The PR touches no provider runtime, attestation, encryption or billing code, so TB-002, TB-009, TB-011 and T-041 are not directly affected.

DeviceLinkForm.tsx (head lines ~9 and ~45) now always adds `purpose` to the JSON body POSTed to /api/device/approve. The value defaults to "provider"; the link page derives it from the ?purpose= query parameter (the page source was not supplied). The approve proxy forwards the raw body unchanged to coordinator /v1/device/approve (account-proxy-contracts.test.ts head 55-63).

Security rests on the platform backend. Per the changelog, it binds each user_code to its purpose and rejects mismatches ("authorization purpose does not match this code"). An attacker-crafted ?purpose= value therefore only changes UI copy; it cannot widen a grant. That backend is platform-owned and its source was not supplied.

For desktop_account, the UI shows success only if the response echoes purpose == desktop_account. This is fail-safe messaging.

The read-only and 30-day claims in the UI copy ("cannot start providers, manage API keys, or withdraw funds") are statements about scopes the backend must enforce. They are not enforced here; the next pass should verify the platform scope enforcement if it is in scope.

No token handling changed. The bearer token still comes from the Privy session, and a missing token aborts before fetch (device-link.test.tsx 99-106).

The phishability of the device-code consent flow is a pre-existing property of that flow.

Coverage limit: console-ui/src/app/link/page.tsx was not supplied. Its handling of the query parameter (whitelisting) is unseen. Any non-whitelisted string would be sent upstream and should be rejected by the server.
